title: An auxiliary expression vanishes at zero
statement: The real-valued expression $x^2 + x + \log(1 - x)$ takes the value $0$ at $x = 0$; that is, $0^2 + 0 + \log(1 - 0) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: none (a closed identity evaluated at zero)
replaced:
The evaluation $0^2 + 0 + \log(1-0) = 0$ establishes the base case for the
Taylor bound, confirming that $h(0)=0$ in the derivative argument for
\texttt{neg\_log\_one\_sub\_two\_mul\_le\_two\_sq}.
